# PyAutoLens Assistant

> **If your AI can't browse GitHub, paste this entire file into the chat as context.** It is
> the front door of the PyAutoLens Assistant — an AI assistant for doing strong-lens science
> with PyAutoLens (agent instructions, task skills, and a reference wiki in one repo you drive
> by conversation). It routes you by intent: start a chat session, see what the assistant can
> do, read the reference, or jump to runnable examples.

Every link below is an **absolute raw URL**, so it is fetchable from a chat that has browsing
but no repository connector. (Relative links and `blob/` page URLs are the two things that
reliably fail there — `blob/` returns a JavaScript shell, not the file.)

## Pick your harness

| You are using | Do this |
|---|---|
| **A coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) | Clone the repo and open the agent inside it. `AGENTS.md` loads automatically; nothing below is needed. |
| **Chat with a GitHub connector** (ChatGPT or Claude on a paid plan) | Enable the connector, then use the bootstrap prompt below. |
| **Chat with browsing but no connector** | Use the bootstrap prompt below — it points at raw URLs, which fetch fine. |
| **Chat with neither** (incl. ChatGPT Free) | Paste [`llms-chat.txt`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/llms-chat.txt) — a self-contained ~6k-token bundle carrying the rules and the current API surface. |
| **A Claude Project, or a custom GPT** | Upload the files in [`chat_pack/`](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/tree/main/chat_pack) as knowledge. |

Only the paid-subscription CLI coding agents **Claude Code** and **Codex** are supported today; setup
pages for each live under `docs/setup/`. The archived guide to every other platform (kept for
reinstatement once conversation-assistant support returns):
**[`docs/archive/CHOOSING_YOUR_AI_TOOL.md`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/docs/archive/CHOOSING_YOUR_AI_TOOL.md)**

## Bootstrap prompt

Naming this file explicitly **matters**: an assistant does not reliably find `llms.txt` on its
own, and results are markedly better when it is pointed here first.

```text
Start by reading the front door of the autolens_assistant repository:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/llms.txt

Follow its read order (AGENTS_CHAT.md → the relevant skill → wiki) and its API rules,
then use the repository to answer my PyAutoLens questions. First tell me whether
you can actually read llms.txt — if you can't, say so plainly and don't answer
from memory.
```

## How to behave in chat

Read order: [AGENTS_CHAT.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/AGENTS_CHAT.md)
(chat-mode rules; the executable-harness version is
[AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/AGENTS.md)) →
[skills/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/skills/README.md)
→ the relevant skill → [wiki/](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/tree/main/wiki).

**Lead by engaging.** Ask what the user is trying to do, ask them to describe or plot their
data (you can't inspect files on their machine), plan the model, and draft the scripts — do
this *first*, and never open a reply with what you can't do. The assistant can also route to
examples, explain lensing, and review pasted scripts / errors / figures. It cannot run code or
guarantee drafts against the installed PyAutoLens version, so switching to a local coding agent
(Claude Code, Codex, or Codex web with the repo connected) is the step for **actually running
the fit or iterating live** — raise that handoff when execution becomes the blocker, not as an
opening disclaimer.

**⚠️ API currency — read before writing any PyAutoLens code.** Older PyAutoLens releases are
heavily represented in model training data and their API is **out of date**. Do **not** write
PyAutoLens from memory — mirror the exact calls shown in the relevant
[`skills/`](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/tree/main/skills) file, and check
symbols against the generated
[current API surface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/chat_pack/01_api_surface.md).
The single most common stale error: **plotting is functional now.** Use
`aplt.subplot_fit_imaging(fit=fit, output_path=..., output_filename=..., output_format="png")`
and `aplt.subplot_imaging_dataset(dataset=..., ...)`. The old object-oriented plotters —
`aplt.FitImagingPlotter`, `aplt.ImagingPlotter`, `aplt.TracerPlotter`, `aplt.MatPlot2D`,
`aplt.Output` — have been **removed**; never emit them. If you can't point at a `skills/`
example for a call, say it's unverified rather than guessing.

## Agent instructions (canonical)

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/AGENTS.md): safety rules, modes, and repository conventions — the source of truth for harnesses that can execute.
- [AGENTS_CHAT.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/AGENTS_CHAT.md): the chat-mode subset — the same rules, minus everything that needs a shell.

## What it can do

- [skills/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/skills/README.md): one-line index of every task skill.

## Reference

- [wiki/core/index.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/wiki/core/index.md): curated PyAuto* reference — stack, lensing concepts, API catalogues, operations.
- [wiki/literature/index.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_assistant/main/wiki/literature/index.md): strong-lensing science wiki — concepts, named entities (surveys, lenses), bibliography. **Large — fetch single pages, never the whole tree.**

## Runnable examples & tutorials (elsewhere)

- [autolens_workspace navigator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PyAutoLabs/autolens_workspace/main/llms.txt): paste-friendly task router for end-to-end example scripts and notebooks.
- [HowToLens](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/HowToLens): from-first-principles strong-lensing lecture series.
